newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines sees tamed inflation as peso recovers.
newsitem.headline: Philippines sees tamed inflation as peso recovers.

text.p: Philippine inflation is projected to remain at an average of six to seven percent this year, as the peso slowly recovers to 28.00 to the dollar level on Thursday, central bank governor Gabriel Singson said.
"I expect the inflation of six to seven percent in our programme with the IMF to be within reach, even with the increase in the price of the dollar," Singson said in a news conference.
He said the low first-half inflation of 4.6 percent would help bring down the full-year average.
He denied widespread media reports that a worst-case scenario would give an average of 8.5 percent for the year.
"Even for the second half, it (the number) is high," he said.
In May, the government lowered its own target to 5.2-5.7 percent for this year. Last year, inflation averaged at 8.4 percent.

Fears of runaway inflation swept across the country when the peso fell to its 45-month low of 30.00 to the peso early this week, following the de facto devaluation announced last Friday. Before that the peso was hovering around 26.40.
Philippines relies heavily on imported crude oil and other basic commodities such as wheat and rice to feed.
Singson said speculative pressure on the peso has been easing lately.
"The rate will slowly go down and the average for the third quarter will probably be at 27 to 28 pesos to the dollar," he said.
The central bank projects the peso will recover further in the fourth quarter to 26.50 to 27.00, mostly due to the influx of foreign exchange from the overseas Filipino workers.
On Thursday, the peso closed at 28.00 to the dollar after vacillating within 27.65 and 29.50 throughout the moderately-traded session.
As the speculative pressure on the peso ebbs, Singson said interest rates should also decline.
The central bank's benchmark overnight borrowing rate was cut to 28.0 percent on Wednesday from 32 percent. It was expected to be reduced further in the coming days.
The overnight borrowing rate influences the domestic yield curve. Treasury bill rates have gone to their two-year highs after the overnight borrowing rates were raised to ward off peso speculators.
Despite the uncertainties in the foreign exchange market, President Fidel Ramos said that there was no need to revise the economic targets for this year.
The National Statistics Office earlier announced a further slowdown in the merchandise trade deficit, as exports outpaced imports in the first five months of the year.
Trade deficit narrowed to $4.727 billion in the first five months of the year from $5.090 billion in the same period last year.
Exports grew by 22.9 percent to $9.571 billion, while imports up by only 11.0 percent to $12.879 billion.
